official_sources.title: GDAL affine geotransform and pixel-center convention
official_sources.finding: GDAL defines a six-coefficient affine transform from pixel/line space to georeferenced coordinates; raster coordinates run from the upper-left pixel corner at (0,0), and the upper-left pixel center is (0.5,0.5).
official_sources.limitation: The affine transform locates samples horizontally but does not establish raster value validity, vertical datum, measurement accuracy, or parcel inclusion.

official_sources.title: GDAL inverse geotransform fail-closed behavior
official_sources.finding: GDALInvGeoTransform converts georeferenced coordinates back to fractional pixel/line coordinates and explicitly fails when the affine equation is uninvertible.
official_sources.limitation: An invertible transform can still be semantically wrong because of incorrect CRS, axis, PixelIsPoint interpretation, stale metadata, or unreviewed rounding.

official_sources.title: GDAL GetGeoTransform success-state requirement
official_sources.finding: GDAL GetGeoTransform returns a status and may return the identity coefficients even when georeferencing retrieval fails, so coefficient values alone cannot prove valid georeferencing.
official_sources.limitation: A successful affine transform still requires exact CRS, dimensions, raster type, source identity and round-trip checks.

official_sources.title: OGC GeoTIFF raster-space type requirements
official_sources.finding: GeoTIFF 1.1 defines GTRasterTypeGeoKey values for PixelIsArea and PixelIsPoint and strongly recommends the key for accurate raster-space interpretation.
official_sources.limitation: The raster-space type describes sample support semantics; it does not by itself prove producer correctness or define parcel boundary inclusion.

official_sources.title: GDAL PixelIsPoint half-pixel interpretation
official_sources.finding: GDAL RFC 33 explains that GeoTIFF PixelIsPoint tie-point interpretation requires a half-pixel adjustment when converted to GDAL's area-based geotransform model and documents compatibility risks for older files.
official_sources.limitation: Legacy files and configuration overrides can change apparent positioning; file provenance, GDAL version and relevant configuration must be pinned.

official_sources.title: Rasterio center/corner coordinate and index operations
official_sources.finding: Rasterio xy returns pixel centers by default and can return ul, ur, ll or lr corners; index converts coordinates to row and column using an explicit rounding operator.
official_sources.limitation: Default center and floor-like indexing must not silently choose parcel support at exact boundaries; the operator and tie policy must be explicit.

official_sources.title: Rasterio fractional windows and deterministic rounding
official_sources.finding: Rasterio windows may have fractional offsets and lengths; round_offsets floors offsets, round_lengths rounds lengths, and window_index rounds starts down and stops up for array slicing.
official_sources.limitation: Automatic rounding can include extra cells; exact geometry masking is still required after conservative window expansion.

official_sources.title: Rasterio window bounds, crop and intersection behavior
official_sources.finding: Rasterio exposes window bounds, dataset cropping, intersection, union and window-relative affine transforms, enabling explicit reconciliation of requested and clipped pixel extents.
official_sources.limitation: Rectangular window intersection is only a candidate read extent; it does not replace exact parcel geometry, mask polarity or sample-center support tests.
